extensions.name: claude-code
extensions.description: Claude Code for VS Code: Harness the power of Claude Code without leaving your IDE

works: Claude Code in the terminal: the ✻ Claude Code status bar item and Claude Code: Open in Terminal start claude in a terminal tab to the right of the editor
claude connects to Diode (/ide): it sees the selected text and the file you are in
Ctrl+Alt+K inserts an @-mention of the current file and selected lines into the claude prompt
claude reads the editor's diagnostics: errors and warnings from your language servers
claude started by hand in any Diode terminal connects too: the extension sets CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT in every terminal
Proposed edits open as a diff tab: accept with ✓ (or edit the proposal and save), reject with ↺ or by closing the tab
limits: Needs the claude CLI on your PATH and your own Claude account: in terminal mode the extension runs claude from PATH, and you sign in inside claude
The chat panel does not open: it is a webview, and Diode has none by design. Commands that need it do nothing: Open in New Tab, Open in New Window, Open in Side Bar, and Alt+K (use Ctrl+Alt+K)
Ctrl+Esc works only in terminals with the kitty keyboard protocol; elsewhere use the status bar item or the command palette

extensions.name: catppuccin-vsc
extensions.description: 🦌 Soothing pastel theme for VSCode

extensions.name: vscode-markdownlint
extensions.description: Markdown linting and style checking for Visual Studio Code

works: Diagnostics in Problems and in the editor, while typing
Quick fixes, Format Document, fix on save and the fix all command
Lint Workspace task, focus mode, toggling linting and live reload of the config file
limits: The markdownlint-disable comment snippets are not offered: Diode has no extension snippets so far

extensions.description: EditorConfig Support for Visual Studio Code

extensions.name: todo-tree
extensions.description: Show TODO, FIXME, etc. comment tags in a tree view

works: The TODOS view in the sidebar: tags (TODO, FIXME, BUG, HACK, XXX, [ ], [x]) across the workspace and open files, as a tree of folders, files and tag lines, or flat, tags only and grouped by tag
Enter or a click on a tag line opens the file at that line
The tree updates as you edit an open file and when you open or save a file with a tag; Todo Tree: Refresh rescans the workspace
Filters and views from the node context menu and the command palette: Filter Tree, Hide This File, Only Show This Folder, Reset All Filters, Expand Tree, Collapse Tree
The tag count in the status bar (todo-tree.general.statusBar) and in tree labels (todo-tree.tree.showCountsInTree)
limits: Tags are not highlighted in the editor text (todo-tree.highlights): Diode draws extension decorations only in the gutter and the overview ruler
The container has no icon in the sidebar switcher, it is labeled with text; tree nodes have no tooltips
Tag lines have no icon by default: the extension draws its tag icons as SVG files. A codicon set as the tag's icon (todo-tree.highlights.customHighlight, e.g. "$(flame)") is shown
Badges (todo-tree.tree.showBadges) show file icons, but no Git or Problems decorations on file nodes
The command palette shows all Todo Tree commands, including the ones the extension hides from it

extensions.name: supermaven
extensions.description: The fastest copilot.

works: Inline completions (ghost text): Tab accepts, Esc dismisses
The extension downloads and runs its own completion engine
Status bar entry with the engine state
Sign-in to the free tier: the prompt asks for your email in a quick input
limits: Chat panel does not open: it is a webview, and Diode has none by design
Commands that need that panel do nothing: New Chat, History, Settings, Select Model, Add to Chat, Edit with Supermaven, Fix with Supermaven
Pro sign-in goes through a browser, which a remote or headless terminal may not have

extensions.name: vscode-buf
extensions.description: Visual Studio Code support for Buf

works: Protocol Buffers syntax highlighting for .proto files and buf.yaml / buf.gen.yaml
Diagnostics in Problems, hover with doc comments, go to definition (F12), completion and formatting from the Buf language server
Well-known types (google/protobuf/*.proto) resolve without extra setup
The buf binary is downloaded automatically on first start when it is not on PATH; status bar shows the Buf version
Buf: Init, Buf: Build and Start/Stop Buf Language Server from the command palette; logs in Output → Buf
limits: Buf: List available lint rules and List available breaking change detection rules fail: they open the list as a new untitled document, which Diode cannot create from an extension yet

The Import module command: a quick pick of modules, the statement goes in at the cursor
devDependencies through npm-intellisense.scanDevDependencies; an empty list without a package.json

extensions.name: prettier-vscode
extensions.description: Code formatter using prettier

works: Format Document (Ctrl+K Ctrl+E) and Format Selection (Ctrl+K Ctrl+F) on every language Prettier supports
Markdown, JSON, YAML, CSS/LESS/SCSS and HTML — languages no language server formats in Diode
Format on save via editor.formatOnSave
Bundled Prettier, or the prettier from your project's node_modules when there is one
.prettierrc / .editorconfig are read, and re-read when you edit them
Status bar entry with the formatter state; its log is in Output → Prettier
limits: Prettier: Create Configuration File does nothing — it opens a folder picker, which Diode does not have yet
No way to choose between formatters: Diode has no editor.defaultFormatter, and on TypeScript/JavaScript Prettier wins over the built-in TypeScript formatter

extensions.name: auto-close-tag
extensions.description: Automatically add HTML/XML close tag, same as Visual Studio IDE or Sublime Text

extensions.name: go
extensions.description: Rich Go language support for Visual Studio Code

works: Diagnostics from gopls, in the editor and the Problems panel
Hover with doc comments from other packages, go to definition (F12) and completion, including auto-import of the package you complete from
Format on save and organize imports on save, as the extension configures them for Go files
gopls is installed by the extension itself (go install) when it is not found; the Go version shows in the status bar
Go commands from the command palette, such as Go: Toggle Test File and Go: Locate Configured Go Tools; logs in Output → Go
limits: Requires the Go toolchain: the go binary on your PATH (or go.goroot). Without it the extension shows "Failed to find the go binary" with a link to the download page and does not start
Debugging does not work: Diode has no debugger
Tests are not shown in a Testing view and there are no run test / debug test code lenses yet — run go test in the terminal
The Go welcome page and the pprof profile viewer are webviews, and do nothing

extensions.name: terraform
extensions.description: Syntax highlighting and autocompletion for Terraform

works: Syntax highlighting for Terraform, tfvars, Terraform Stacks and test files
Hover, completion with provider schemas, go to definition (F12) and diagnostics in Problems from the bundled terraform-ls
limits: HCP Terraform, Providers and Module Calls views do not render yet: Diode has no extension tree views so far
Sign-in to HCP Terraform is not supported yet
Formatting and the init/validate/plan commands need the terraform CLI on PATH, as in VS Code

extensions.name: regionfolder
extensions.description: Provides folding for text wrapped with #region comments in VS Code.

extensions.name: java
extensions.displayName: Language Support for Java(TM) by Red Hat
extensions.description: Java Linting, Intellisense, formatting, refactoring, Maven/Gradle support and more...

works: Diagnostics from the Eclipse JDT language server, in the editor and the Problems panel
Hover with Javadoc read from dependency jars, and completion from the project and the JDK
Go to definition into your own code and into library sources, opened read-only
Find All References, code actions and quick fixes, and formatting
Source generators that ask you to pick: Override/Implement Methods, Generate Constructors, toString
Maven and Gradle projects are imported by the server; its state shows in the status bar
limits: The formatter settings editor does not open: it is a custom editor (a webview), and Diode has none by design — edit java.format.* in settings.json instead
Documentation previews and the Change Signature dialog are webviews too, and do nothing
Debugging, test running and the Java Projects view are not in this extension: they need the rest of the Extension Pack for Java, which Diode does not support
The universal build needs JDK 21 or newer on your PATH or in JAVA_HOME; the platform builds bundle a JRE and need nothing

extensions.name: trailing-spaces
extensions.description: Highlight trailing spaces and delete them in a flash!

works: Trailing Spaces: Delete and Delete - Modified Lines Only
Trimming on save with trailing-spaces.trimOnSave, undo brings the spaces back
limits: Trailing spaces are not highlighted in the text: Diode does not paint text decorations from extensions yet, so the Highlight command and the backgroundColor and borderColor settings have no visible effect

extensions.name: bazel-java-tihonove
extensions.description: Bazel support for Java Linting, Intellisense, formatting, refactoring and more... Fork of sfdc.bazel-vscode-java with Bazel 9 / bzlmod fixes.

works: Bazel workspaces are imported by the Java language server: classpath between targets, diagnostics, completion and navigation across //packages
Synchronize Projects with Bazel, Refresh Bazel Projects (after branch switch / pull), Update Classpath — from the command palette
The Bazel Build Status terminal with the synchronization log (Java: Show Bazel Build Status)
Language Support for Java by Red Hat is installed automatically as a dependency
.bazelproject project views, BUILD / Starlark syntax highlighting, buildifier formatting
limits: The Bazel Targets tree view is not shown: Diode does not render extension tree views yet
Run targets from IntelliJ run configurations are not executed: there is no task runner (tasks.executeTask)
Needs bazel (or bazelisk) on PATH and a Bazel 9 workspace with WORKSPACE or WORKSPACE.bazel present
